verdict.rationale: The Drive API exposes a permissions resource on every file, folder and shared drive. Permissions can target user, group, domain or anyone, with roles from owner to reader, so link visibility is programmable through the product's own API. Creating and revoking permissions is implied by that resource model rather than shown as explicit create/delete operations, and nothing in the evidence covers password protection or expiry on shared links. Missing for 10: password-protected links, link expiry settings, explicit documentation of creating and revoking permissions via the API.

support.subject: As a developer, sharing is programmable — shared links with visibility, password, and expiry settings can be created and revoked via the API

citations.quote: Each resource identifies the permission for a specific type (user, group, domain, anyone) and role (owner, organizer, fileOrganizer, writer, commenter, reader).
Every Google Drive file, folder, and shared drive has associated `permissions` resources.
A permission grants a user, group, domain, or the world access to a file or a folder hierarchy.
